page: Microsoft Azure D64lds_v7 is an x86_64 compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at a rated clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem is equipped with 480 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and supports vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual CPU.

Integrated local storage is delivered via 3780 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, providing fast, localized scratch and caching throughput without reliance on external block devices. The instance features zero attached GPUs and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark evaluations show strong multi-core throughput, with stress-ng multi-core testing placing in the top 25 percent alongside high-tier results in PassMark CPU and encryption benchmarks. Memory subsystem metrics reflect high cached throughput, achieving 4705.01 GB/sec on small read blocks, though PassMark overall memory scores remain in the average bracket.

Data handling and transactional benchmarks demonstrate high density execution, highlighted by 109.21 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and strong database operation results. Accelerated matrix extensions also contribute to above-average prompt processing across 7B and 70B parameter language models. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio prioritizes compute concurrency over memory density, making the instance cost-efficient for core-heavy parallel jobs rather than memory-heavy footprints.

The D64lds_v7 is suitable for high-concurrency computational workloads that benefit from local NVMe temporary storage. Primary applications include multi-threaded batch processing, distributed caching layers, data compression pipelines, build and continuous integration systems, and compute-bound microservice hosting.
